objective.statement: Fix the credential leak where connecting with a bad database URL logs the full URL including the password, by redacting secrets in log output and adding a regression test proving no secret reaches the logs.
objective.success_definition: Connecting with a bad database URL no longer logs the password; a regression test proves no secret reaches the logs; the log line format is unchanged so existing consumers keep parsing; no new dependencies are introduced; no request bodies are logged anywhere.

goals.statement: Redact secrets in log output so that the password in a bad database URL (and secrets generally) never appear in logs.
acceptance: Connecting with a bad database URL produces a log line with the password redacted
No secret value appears in log output

goals.statement: Add a regression test proving no secret reaches the logs.
acceptance: A test exists that asserts logged output contains no secret
The test fails if a secret is written to the logs

goals.statement: Keep the log line format unchanged so existing consumers keep parsing.
acceptance: The log line format is identical to before apart from the redaction of the secret
Existing log consumers can still parse the log lines

constraints.statement: No new dependencies may be added.
Do not log request bodies anywhere.

include: Database connection error logging path where the full URL including the password is currently logged
Redaction of secrets in log output
Regression test proving no secret reaches the logs

assumptions.statement: The exact files/modules to modify are not named in the task; the change is assumed to be confined to the database connection error logging path and its tests.
"Secrets" means at minimum the password in the database URL; whether other secret types elsewhere in log output must also be redacted is unspecified.
An existing test suite/framework exists to which the regression test can be added, consistent with the no-new-dependencies constraint.

open_questions.question: Which files contain the logging call that emits the database URL, and where should the regression test live?
Should redaction cover only the database URL password, or all secrets in any log output?
options: All secrets in all log output

verification.spec: Run the new regression test that connects with a bad database URL and inspects captured log output.
verification.expected: The test passes with redaction in place and fails if any secret reaches the logs.

verification.spec: Connect with a bad database URL and compare the emitted log line against the previous format.
verification.expected: The password is redacted and the log line format is otherwise unchanged and still parseable by existing consumers.

deliverables.description: Redaction of secrets in log output so a bad database URL's password is never logged.
Regression test proving no secret reaches the logs.

factors: Credential leak is a live security issue; incomplete redaction leaves secrets exposed in logs
Changing the log line format could break existing log consumers
Redaction logic must not itself introduce new logging of secrets
